description: The UNLOCK statement (ISO 14.9.47; UNLOCK file [RECORD[S]]) - releases every record lock this connector holds on the file. A COBOL-2002 introduction; 0900 below 2002. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): ANSI X3.23-1985 has no record locking and UNLOCK is no 1985 reserved word (§1985:IV.8 runs UNIT, UNSTRING: its rows '| OFF | REDEFINES | SORT | UNIT |' and '| OMITTED | REEL | SORT-MERGE | UNSTRING |'); §2002:14.8.43 reads 'The UNLOCK statement explicitly releases any record locks associated with a file connector' (§2002:14.8.43.3 GR1: 'Any record locks associated with the file connector referenced by file-name-1 are released by the execution of the UNLOCK statement'), §2002:F.1 item 6 adds UNLOCK to the reserved words and its item 2 the status UNLOCK can return ('I-O status 42 has been expanded to include the case in which an attempt is made to UNLOCK a file that is not in the open mode'), and §2002:F.2 item 111 states the facility: 'Record locking allows control of record access for shared files.' §2014:14.9.43 and §2014:14.9.43.3 GR1 carry it, so 2014 = 2023.

IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. ROWUN.
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
       FILE-CONTROL.
           SELECT F ASSIGN TO "f.dat" ORGANIZATION IS SEQUENTIAL.
       DATA DIVISION.
       FILE SECTION.
       FD F.
       01 R PIC X(8).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           UNLOCK F.
           STOP RUN.
